title: New Machine Sales
summary: Loaders, excavators, dozers, haulers and graders supplied to your specification, inspected and handed over on site.
lede: We sell the machine the job needs, not the machine that happens to be in the yard.
body: Every enquiry starts with the work, not the model list: what you are moving, how far, how many hours a week, and what the ground does when it rains. That decides bucket size, tyre compound, counterweight and drivetrain long before it decides a price.
Each machine leaves our workshop with a documented pre-delivery inspection, the attachments fitted and a handover on your site with the operators who will run it.

title: Certified Used Equipment
summary: Low-hour machines put through a 140-point inspection, with the report in your hands before you pay a deposit.
lede: A used machine is only worth buying when somebody has written down what is wrong with it.
body: Our certified used process is the one we use on trade-ins we intend to keep in our own rental fleet. A 140-point inspection, oil sampling on every circuit, undercarriage measured rather than eyeballed, and a written report you read before you commit.
Anything outside tolerance is repaired before the machine is listed. We would rather carry the cost than discount a fault and argue about it later.
deliverables: Repair record for work carried out

title: Genuine Parts and Attachments
summary: Filters, wear parts, undercarriage and attachments held in stock, with same-day despatch on stocked lines.
lede: A stopped machine costs more per hour than the part that stopped it.
body: We hold service kits, cutting edges, teeth, pins, bushes and undercarriage for every model we sell, and we despatch stocked lines the same day they are ordered.
On attachments we fit as well as sell: hoses, couplers, control valves and the in-cab switching, plumbed in our workshop and pressure tested before the machine leaves.

title: Field Service and Maintenance
summary: Mobile technicians with fully stocked service vans, on scheduled plans or on call when a machine goes down.
lede: Servicing on a calendar costs less than repairs on a phone call.
body: Our service vans carry the filters, fluids and common failure parts for the machines on our books, so a first visit is usually a fix rather than a diagnosis followed by a second visit.
Planned maintenance contracts set the intervals against machine hours rather than months, with oil sampling at each service so wear is caught while it is still a filter change.
deliverables: Service history and oil trend reporting

title: Fleet Rental and Leasing
summary: Short-term hire for a peak and long-term lease for a contract, both with service and breakdown cover included.
lede: Own the machines you run every week. Hire the ones you run for a season.
body: Short-term hire covers the peak without putting another machine on your balance sheet, and it comes with servicing and breakdown cover so a hired machine is never your maintenance problem.
Long-term leases are written against contract length, with a fixed monthly figure that includes scheduled servicing and an agreed hour allowance.
deliverables: Rate schedule by machine and term

title: Finance and Trade-In
summary: Hire purchase, lease purchase and trade-in valuations, quoted against the machine's real residual value.
lede: The purchase price is one number. What the machine is worth in five years is the other one.
body: We quote finance against the residual we would actually pay for the machine at the end of the term, which is why our monthly figures survive a comparison with a broker's.
Trade-ins are valued on hours, service history and undercarriage condition, and the valuation holds for thirty days.

title: Operator and Technician Training
summary: Machine-specific operator training and workshop courses for the technicians who keep the fleet running.
lede: The same machine burns a third more fuel in the wrong hands.
body: Operator training is run on your machine, on your site, on the material you actually move. Most of the saving comes from loading technique and idle discipline rather than anything on a screen.
Technician courses run in our workshop and cover diagnostics, hydraulic testing and driveline work on the models in your fleet.
deliverables: Fuel burn before and after report

title: Transport and Site Logistics
summary: Low-loader delivery, machine moves between sites and abnormal-load planning handled end to end.
lede: Getting the machine there is part of selling it.
body: We run our own low-loaders and arrange the permits, escorts and routing for abnormal loads, so a delivery date is a date rather than an estimate.
Site-to-site moves are booked the same way, whether or not the machine came from us.
deliverables: Proof of delivery with condition photos
